_comment: Funnel and activation-window configuration.
ACTIVATION WINDOW
A referral counts as an activation only if it lands between
window_start_days and window_end_days of the customer's installation.
Default -3 .. +90: wide enough to cover installation, commissioning,
subsidy disbursal and the first zero bill, which are the high points for
most customers.
BLINDSPOT: referrals before window_start_days are excluded entirely.
Deep pre-installation referrals carry noise (they predate the customer
having a working system), so they are neither activations nor counted
anywhere in the activation metrics. They remain visible in the lifetime
is_referrer flag so the two can be compared.
SUB-WINDOWS
Reporting buckets inside the activation window. The last one is bounded
by commissioning: whichever of (window end, commissioning) comes first.
CX RECOMMENDED / IDV
PLACEHOLDERS. enabled=false means the ETL does not query any source and
the dashboard renders the column as a dash rather than a zero -- a zero
would read as 'we did none', which is not what we know.
When the real source arrives, set enabled=true and fill in `source`.

idv             NOW WIRED UP -- see sql/04_idv.sql. It is a
RECONNECTION MEETING in meeting_metrics_history, one row
per SSEID by latest updatedAt, exactly as card 5318.
IDV WINDOW: deliberately none, matching card 5318. About a fifth of the
meetings counted sit outside +/-3 days of the installation, so these are
slightly broader than 'installation day' read literally. If a window is
wanted later it belongs in transform.py, next to the activation window it
would have to agree with -- not in the extract.
Rejected alternatives: usertasks key SC_IDV_01 has 45 rows in total;
meeting_type 'site_visit' covers 1,611 SSEIDs against
reconnection_meeting's 10,241; user_slots_visits_visits is dead.
